target_customer: Cash based micro and small businesses in Uganda needing short term working capital
problem: Micro business owners borrow from informal lenders or family because they have no digital transaction history. Numida scores and lends to them through an app.
business_model: lender earning interest on unsecured working capital loans, funded by equity and debt

founders.name: Mina Shahid
previous_startups: lending company in Ghana that failed (with Numida's CTO, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: two time founder, Egyptian and Canadian, worked in Uganda, Ghana, Zambia and Colombia.

founders.name: Catherine Denis
education: Systems Design Engineering, University of Waterloo
founders.background_notes: YC page: 8+ years in Uganda, Rwanda, Burkina Faso, Mali, Haiti and Colombia.

founders.name: Ben Best
founders.background_notes: Named as cofounder by TechCrunch (2022); not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring for cash based businesses without digital history plus mobile money disbursement and collection; standard fintech engineering with hard data problems.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data on cash businesses compounds, and a funded loan book with good collections is hard to copy quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mobile lenders targeted consumers with smaller loans; the sources opened show no copying or acquisition of Numida.

market_need_then: In 2017 Numida was raising from angels and winning Seedstars Kampala, targeting credit constrained Ugandan entrepreneurs who relied on informal lenders. Loans of $100 to $5,000 were later repaid in a month at 10 to 16 percent interest per TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand coverage is limited to fundraising press; no source discusses the name, identity or community.

pivots.from: free personal financial management app with loans unlocked by usage
pivots.to: direct working capital loans to micro businesses
pivots.why: Not stated; the 2017 Bizcommunity article describes the app model and the 2022 TechCrunch article describes the loan model.

outcome_analysis: Numida is the first Ugandan YC company and kept growing, lending $20M in working capital by September 2022 and raising $12.3M in equity and debt, with monthly issuance growing from $250K to $2M. Founder market fit in East Africa and proprietary repayment data helped, while macro and currency risk in Uganda remain. It is active with 115 staff.
notes: TechCrunch says the $12.3M round was equity plus debt; the $7.3M equity figure comes from TechCabal and CNBC Africa snippets and equals 12.3 minus 5. Round stage 'other' because outlets call it a pre Series A. Seed date is only 2021 and the $2.3M seed was seen in several outlets via search results, not opened. CB Insights lists a $1.95M raise in December 2024; unverified and not recorded. Founding year 2016 on YC page, 2017 in TechCrunch. Bizcommunity (2017) says Numida had raised $140K from angels. Pivot is inferred from two dated descriptions and the wording should be treated as approximate. numida.com redirected, so the site was not read. Competitor list emptied: Tala, Branch, JUMO and informal lenders were all sourced to a 2017-08 Bizcommunity article, five years before the W22 batch, and the TechCrunch 2022-09 article (opened) names no competitors. No sources dated near the batch were found. as_of was left unchanged.
